I found one minor regression in the uncommitted change to `bash_completionsV2.go`, at line 194. Otherwise it looks fine. I only read the diff and the surrounding function. I didn't run any completions.

**Empty completions are no longer filtered out** (`bash_completionsV2.go:194`)
- The old code ran `compgen -W "$comp" -- "$cur"` and skipped the line when the result was empty. That also dropped any line whose text before the tab was empty.
- The new check, `[[ $comp == "$cur"* ]]`, passes when `$comp` is empty and `$cur` is empty. A line like `\tsome description` is then added to `COMPREPLY` as a blank candidate.
- This is an edge case. It needs the program to emit a completion line with an empty value, or a blank line in the output.
- A guard fixes it: `[[ -n $comp && $comp == "$cur"* ]] || continue`.

**The two code paths now match differently** (`bash_completionsV2.go:183` and `:194`)
- The no-description path at line 183 still uses `compgen -W "$out"`. That splits on whitespace and expands `$`, backticks and similar in the completion text.
- The description path now does a literal prefix match.
- The new behavior is arguably more correct, because completions that contain spaces or `$` are no longer mangled when descriptions are present. But the same completion can now behave differently depending on whether any line in `$out` has a description.
